name: Longer Ray5 5W
tagline: 5W Compact fixed-focus diode: simple desk engraver for small projects
tldr: Longer Ray5 5W is the 5W SKU on the Longer longer ray5 line. Longer's compact Ray5 20W diode engraver: verify you are buying the 20W SKU, not the 5W, 10W, or 40W Ray5 listings. Verify optical power on the listing: do not assume combined-watt marketing.

priceRange.note: Official Longer store, Oct 2026: $160 to $520 depending on bundle

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

pros: Lowest price of the Ray5 range: $159.99 basic set on Longer's store (October 2026)
Square 0.08 × 0.08 mm spot, per Longer, for clean text and logos
Low heat and smoke: a gentle first machine for small pieces
cons: A 10 × 10 cm photo fill takes ~44–65 min in our benchmarks
Cutting tops out around 3 mm basswood in practice, at ~2–3 mm/s
Little headroom: most owners outgrow it once they start cutting
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 5W SKU on Longer Ray5. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other power options via the chips before buying.
proTips: Optimize for engraving: lower DPI on photos, higher scan speed on line art after test burns. Air assist still helps clarity. Compare benchmark times on the next tier before assuming you need more power.
primaryUse: Engraving-first desktop diode for makers who prioritize mark quality over cut speed
mainObjective: Detailed engraving on organics and coated metal: occasional thin cuts only

editorialDepth.advantages: Longer Ray5 5W suits makers who sell marks, photos, and gifts more than daily panel cutting. Reasonable open-frame entry price.
editorialDepth.limitations: Skip if you already quote 3 mm+ cutting in production: see 10W, 20W or 40W in the line. Not for cast acrylic or bare metal without spray.

faq.question: What can the Ray5 5W cut?
faq.answer: Longer rates the 5W module for 4 mm basswood in one pass. In our benchmarks a 10 × 10 cm square in 3 mm basswood takes about 22–36 min at 2–3 mm/s, so 3 mm is the practical limit. Paper, card and thin fabric are easy; clear acrylic is impossible.

faq.question: How long does a photo take on the Ray5 5W?
faq.answer: Slow: a filled 10 × 10 cm photo on birch plywood takes about 44–65 min in our benchmarks. The 5W is better suited to text, logos and line art, which engrave far faster than photo fills.

faq.question: Ray5 5W or 10W: is the cheaper one enough?
faq.answer: On Longer's store in October 2026 the basic sets were $159.99 (5W) and $239.99 (10W). For $80 more, the 10W has a finer 0.06 × 0.06 mm spot (against 0.08 × 0.08 mm), is rated for 8 mm basswood in one pass and cuts our 3 mm square in roughly 14–24 min. Keep the 5W only for occasional engraving on the tightest budget.

standoutFeatures.title: Cheapest Ray5
standoutFeatures.body: $159.99 for the basic set, or $229.99 with air assist and honeycomb, on Longer's store in October 2026.

standoutFeatures.title: Upgrade kits
standoutFeatures.body: Longer sells the same machine with a cutting kit or an all-in-one kit with rotary and camera, so you can start small and add parts.
